market_holds: Spot 16.62 at the 18:11 UTC seal; Yahoo showed 16.92 intraday on 11-10. That is close to the 17.52 close before the July print, a full recovery from the 14.43 low after the July drop. Run-up is +4.3% over 5 days and -6.2% over 20 days (sealed baseline). The option chain is unusable: ATM spread is 111% of mid and open interest totals 750. Front IV of 115.8% would imply an event move of about 14-18%, but I discount that. The usual move is a 5.78% median close-to-close over 7 prints. The close-to-next-open move, which is this window, was positive on 6 of 9 prints since 2024-08 (own arithmetic, Yahoo bars): +10.1, +5.98, +2.9, +0.9, +0.1, -7.7 and -11.4 on the amc prints, +3.7 and +4.4 on the bmo prints. Consensus for FQ4 is revenue $340.3M (guide $325-355M, including about $24M from the 53rd week) and EPS $0.03, with a whisper of $0.01 (Earnings Whispers / finviz preview, 2026-11-03). Sentiment there is 'modestly bearish'. The guide is GAAP gross margin 39-41% with non-GAAP about 120bp higher, a $35M year-on-year memory headwind (about 1,000bp), and adj. EBITDA of -$11M to +$18M. For FY27 the CFO said on the July call that a non-GAAP gross margin near 40%, roughly the low end of the Q4 range, was 'in the ballpark', with the first half lower and opex flat, 'based on what we can see today' in memory prices. Short interest was 12.54M shares at the 10-15 settlement, about 10.6% of shares outstanding and 6.6 days to cover, down from 14.46M at 9-30. The line it trades on is the guidance given on the call (Q1 FY27 and the FY27 margin frame), not the release. In July the stock was +4.3% after hours on the release, then -7.7% at the open and -17.6% at the close once the memory guide came out.
view: The quarter itself is probably fine. Management has delivered at or near the top of its range for eight straight quarters. The new Amp Multi, plus Beam Ultra and Ace Ultra sell-in from 9-29, sit inside a 14-week quarter, so revenue at or above $340M and gross margin near the top of 39-41% are the base case, and the release headline will probably read as a beat. The call decides the window, as it did in July: the Q1 FY27 holiday guide and whether the FY27 gross margin of about 40% survives. Two forces point opposite ways. Against it, memory kept rising after the frame was set. TrendForce (9-30) forecast Q4 conventional DRAM contract prices +10-15% QoQ and NAND +15-20%, DDR4 8Gb contract prices set a record in October, and management has said it has not raised prices on existing products. That makes a trim to the FY27 frame, or a soft Q1 gross margin guide, a live risk. For it, the parts Sonos buys look like they are plateauing. TrendForce's late-October consumer DRAM read was flat to slight increases, MLC NAND contract prices were flat in October after 21 monthly rises, and management guided with mitigation only partly included (500bp annualised). Q1 FY26 is an easy comparison on revenue ($546M, -1% YoY), and about 11% of shares are short, which could squeeze on relief. The stock has already rebuilt the whole July drop, so a reset is not fully in the price. But the July sell-off shows the market already understands that memory is the risk. I cannot show that consensus FY27 numbers lag the memory data, because no dated estimate-revision or consensus gross margin figure was reachable. Net, I lean very slightly to the downside on the guide, offset by a history of positive opens. This is close to a coin flip with a large move either way.

recommendation.reason: The reaction depends on the FY27 gross margin frame and the Q1 guide given on the call. Memory inputs since July point both ways: total DRAM and NAND contract prices are still rising, but consumer DRAM and MLC NAND are flattening. I could not show that consensus lags either one. Without a stale-estimate gap I can measure, no direction reaches 65.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Holding the FY27 non-GAAP gross margin at about 40% or above with Q1 revenue guided above roughly $580M (relief rally and squeeze), against trimming the FY27 frame below 39% because memory costs are rising (a repeat of July).

self_critique: The bear case is that the memory data since July plainly worsen FY27 costs, that management will have to cut the frame or guide Q1 gross margin to about 37%, and that a stock which has rebuilt the whole July drop has room to fall again, so a 'no edge' answer may miss an unpriced downside. The bull case is that this management team sandbags, the consumer memory segments are plateauing, and a short base of about 11% squeezes on any hold of the frame. Both stories are coherent, and I could not find a consensus number that shows which one the price has missed.
approach_notes: P6 (find the line) and the July price path were the most useful: they showed that the call guide, not the release, moves the open. P4 helped stop me treating 'memory rising' as either priced or unpriced, but no estimate-revision data could be reached, so it ended in 'cannot show'.
